verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. First formula: the Lean definition of the angular source carries one extra leading term, -slope·transportW, i.e. the paper's -l·W with W = 1 - L·k̄ (transportW, line 229, uses the averaged drop k̄ exactly as p.135 does). The paper drops it in (A.26) because the axial transition has l = 0; slope_drop proves slope dropLength lam y = 0 for 1 ≤ y ≤ T_d + 1, so on that interval the Lean definition reduces verbatim to -h(1 - 2kη²) + (D + dk)ηJ₀' with k = dropCoefficient c.m y (the coefficient of U = kη) and J₀' = shapeGradient η = 2η/(1+η²). Second formula: angularLag_lower is the paper's bound with the explicit absolute constant c = e^{-3/5}/4, independent of P, λ, h, m; the interval is 0 ≤ y ≤ T for an arbitrary T rather than specifically T_d, and the paper's 'h ≪ e^{-T_d}' is the explicit hypothesis h ≤ e^{-(T+3/5)}/8 (together with h ≤ 1/100 and |η| ≤ 1). angularLag is the solution of the lag equation with the ideal incoming datum (line 246), identified with the actual Q_s history by canonical_Qs_before.
